LESSON: WRITING 8.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES
Strand: Strand 8
Topic 8.3: Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: How can we write interesting animal stories?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression
2. appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: WRITING 8.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION
Subject: INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES · Grade: Grade 7
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information helps you succeed in INDIGENOUS LANGUAGES. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: WRITING 8.3.1 WRITING TO GIVE INFORMATION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression

What this means
In this part you learn to compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment

What this means
In this part you learn to appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information to a partner. (skill: appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression.
3. Practise this skill: appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 7 learner study Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. How can we write interesting animal stories?
2. Why are animal stories important?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Writing 8.3.1 Writing to give information means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: compose an animal story featuring animal characters for self- expression.
5. Be able to: appreciate writing short stories for enjoyment.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
